doc.title: Snooky Young and Gerald Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Lunceford's discipline: outfits and the wrong socks
summary: Lunceford's band was strictly turned out; Snooky was fined for wrong socks.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: And they played those, they did everything. They had a glee club in the band, they had a quartet, trio. And the first thing you do when you join the Jimmie Lunceford band, is go and get measured for seven outfits. Shoes, everything was like, you know, like that.
Yeah, I came in with the wrong socks one day and got a fine. I got a fine. I never wore the wrong socks again. Lunceford looked down, I think we had on white suits, maroon © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-
socks and maroon tie and handkerchief. I think I had on the wrong socks and he saw that with them white shoes. Gotcha.

Wow. That’s amazing. Some of the other fellows have been talking about the difference in band leaders. How Ellington was not, you know, that strict I guess, to put it nicely. But some of the others, like you say, wrong socks, costs you money. Yeah. Tell us about your first big band and how that came about. GW My first big band?
